messages:
Irene B: FYI VentureCorp (acct: VENT-210) invoice INV-9921 for $95,200 is 38 days past due. Card on file declined two retries. I left a voicemail and sent the dunning email.
Mason C: I reached out to my counterpart (oliver@venturecorp.com). They said "we're in M&A, payroll/finance are in flux" and asked us to pause automated collections while they confirm new AP contact.
BillingBot: Autopay failed for INV-9921. Reason: card_expired. Next retry scheduled in 72 hours. Payment link: https://pay.redwood.ai/inv/INV-9921
Irene B: We should avoid full suspension during M&A if possible. Propose: 60-day split (2 installments) or a 3-month installment plan. Offer 1% prompt-payment credit if they pay first installment within 7 days. Need Legal ok for credit.
Sam R (Legal): Temporary credit ok if documented and limited to <2% for a one-time concession. Must capture signed acknowledgement and attach to contract. If they ghost after plan, we escalate.
AM - Priya: From renewal side: they committed to increased seats next quarter; preserving the relationship is high priority. I support a 3-month plan with ACH only.
Irene B: Draft plan: 
```
- Total: $95,200
- Option A: 2 installments: $47,600 due immediately, $47,600 in 30 days
- Option B: 3 installments: $31,734 x3 (rounding on final)
- 1% credit on first installment if paid within 7 days
- ACH/wire preferred; no card retries
- Signed acknowledgment required; if missed payment, immediate right to suspend
```
Mason C: Sending plan to AP now with a request for new AP contact and legal sign-off. I'll ask them to authorize wire for the first installment.
CollectionsBot: Collections outreach paused for VENT-210 until 1743560000 per request. Reminder to resume if no signed plan by then.
BillingBot: Draft invoice INV-9921-PLAN issued. Payment link updated.
Mason C: AP replied: new AP contact is venturepay@acquired-ventures.com. They asked if we can extend to 90 days because of integration timelines. They also asked for our W-9 and a revised invoice to the acquiring entity.
Irene B: 90 days feels long. We can offer 90 days only if they provide a corporate guarantee or exec sign-off. Otherwise stick to 60-90 short split. @Sam R (Legal) ok to require exec sign-off for 90-day term?
Sam R (Legal): Yes, 90-day term acceptable only with an exec-signed promissory note or guarantee from acquiring entity. Document and attach.
AM - Priya: I'll ask VP of Finance to sign if they can confirm acquisition finance will assume liabilities. That should be quick if M&A counsel is aligned.
BillingBot: Payment of $47,600 posted for INV-9921 (txn: WIRE-772211). Remaining balance: $47,600.
Irene B: Payment received. Updating ledger and marking invoice status -> "Partial Payment Plan Active". Collections hold remains until next due date.
Mason C: AP confirmed exec sign-off incoming, sending signed acknowledgement this afternoon.
CollectionsBot: Reminder scheduled: follow-up for remaining balance on 1743799999. If unpaid by 1743799999 escalate to Collections partner.
Irene B: Thanks all. Keep docs in account notes and close interim escalation. If the second payment misses we will reopen and consider collections/legal next steps. :thumbsup:
